question.prompt: If \(n\) is a real number, then the simultaneous system \[ \begin{cases} nx+y=1,\\ ny+z=1,\\ x+nz=1 \end{cases} \] has no solution if and only if \(n\) is equal to

solutions.explanation:
The equations have the same cyclic pattern, so try equal values \(x=y=z=t\). Each equation then becomes
\[
(n+1)t=1.
\]
For every real \(n\ne-1\), the denominator \(n+1\) is nonzero, and choosing
\[
x=y=z=\frac1{n+1}
\]
makes every left side equal to \((n+1)/(n+1)=1\). Thus the system has a solution for every such \(n\).

It remains to test \(n=-1\). Adding the three original equations gives
\[
(n+1)(x+y+z)=3.
\]
When \(n=-1\), this says \(0=3\), which is impossible. Therefore the system has no solution if and only if \(\boxed{n=-1}\), choice A.
